lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For information on customers who accounted for greater than 10% of our consolidated net revenue, see "Note 3: Operating Segments" within Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.
These expenses represented 34.8% of revenue for 2025 and 41.5% of revenue for 2024.
Sales outside the U.S. accounted for 70% of our revenue for 2025.
Moreover, sales outside the U.S. accounted for 70% of our revenue for the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025, with revenue from billings to China contributing 24% of our total revenue.
Collectively, our three largest customers accounted for 43% of our net revenue in 2025, 45% of our net revenue in 2024 and 40% of our net revenue in 2023.

Description of the Matter | The Company's net inventory totaled $11.6 billion as of December 27, 2025, representing 5.5% of total assets. As explained in "Note 2: Accounting Policies" within the consolidated financial statements, the Company computes inventory cost on a first-in, first-out basis, and applies judgment in determining saleability of products and the valuation of inventories. The Company assesses inventory at each reporting date in order to assert that it is recorded at net realizable value, giving consideration to, among other factors: whether the products have achieved the subst
Ireland SCIP | 49% | 49%
Arizona SCIP | 49% | 49%
Mobileye | 20% | 12%
IMS Nanofabrication (IMS Nano) | 32% | 32%
The competitiveness of our product offerings depend on access to manufacturing capacity on leading-edge nodes and advanced packaging.

We intend to remain a leading developer of semiconductor process technology and a major manufacturer of semiconductors, and we plan to continue manufacturing the majority of our products in our own factories.

Our products are designed and marketed by our Intel Products business, which includes our CCG and DCAI operating segments, and are manufactured by our Intel Foundry operating segment and third-party suppliers.
Our development of new process technologies and our manufacturing operations rely on a global supply chain encompassing thousands of suppliers worldwide.

We seek to maintain close relationships with key suppliers to address capacity constraints, quality issues and potential supply chain risks, and actively monitor global supply conditions, diversify sourcing and reduce geographic dependencies where possible.

We design, market, sell and service CPUs and other semiconductor solutions substantially through our Intel Products business that are manufactured by our Intel Foundry business and other suppliers and are incorporated in computing and related end products and services, and utilized globally by consumers, enterprises, governments and educational organizations.
Our business depends on how we engage, manage and reward our people.

Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated by operations and our total cash and short-term investments (defined below), supplemented by undrawn committed credit facilities and other borrowing capacity, recent equity securities agreements and issuances, possible future debt and equity issuances pursuant to our shelf registration statement, monetization of non-core assets and contributions from our Arizona SCIP partner.
Additionally, to the extent we rely upon third party foundries for our products, our margins may be negatively impacted.

To the extent there is any interruption in the supply of tiles manufactured by TSMC or any other third-party foundry supplier, whether as a result of a dispute or otherwise, we would be unable to complete assembly of complete products requiring such tiles until such time as we could design and manufacture replacement tiles and source such tiles from an alternative supplier, which would likely involve a substantial delay given the bespoke design of each tile to the particular manufacturing process utilized.

As an integrated design manufacturer (IDM) with a products business that depends on access to leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing process technologies, or nodes, to produce competitive products, we have historically invested significant capital resources to continually develop new generations of leading-edge nodes and foundry capacity to produce such nodes.
Our operations rely upon a supply chain that is also highly distributed, and with reliance in some instances on supplies or materials available in only one or more geographic areas.
Many of our products depend on suppliers in Taiwan for critical components, including various compute die, that cannot be easily or quickly replaced.
We rely upon a complex global supply chain.
We also rely on suppliers to provide certain components for our products and to manufacture and assemble and test some of our components and products.
As part of our strategy, we expect to continue to rely upon third-party foundries.

We typically have less control over delivery schedules, design and manufacturing co-optimization, yields, quality, product quantities and costs for components and products that are manufactured by third parties.

For certain products, components, services, materials and equipment, we rely on a single or a limited number of suppliers, or upon suppliers in a single location, which can impact the nature, quality, availability and pricing of the products and services available to us.

For example, ASML Holding N.V. (ASML) is currently the sole supplier of EUV lithography tools that we are deploying in our Intel 4, Intel 3, Intel 18A and planned future leading-edge manufacturing process nodes.
Some of our most advanced current and future products are or will be either exclusively manufactured by TSMC or reliant upon critical components, including various compute die, manufactured by TSMC.

In addition, we are often required to rely on third parties, including hardware, software and services vendors, as well as our customers and end users, to develop and/or deploy mitigation techniques, and the availability, effectiveness and performance impact of mitigation techniques can depend solely or in part on the actions of these third parties in determining whether, when, and how to develop and deploy mitigations.
We rely on IP law—as well as confidentiality and licensing agreements with our customers, employees, technology development partners and others—to protect our IP and IP rights.
We rely on access to third-party IP, which may not be available to us on commercially reasonable terms, if at all.
We depend on many distributors to help us create end-customer demand, provide technical support and other value-added services to customers, fill customer orders and stock our products.

At times, we rely on one or more key distributors for a product, and a material change in our relationship with one or more of these distributors or their failure to perform as expected could reduce our revenue.
Investors should not rely on them as statements of fact.

s.t: The carrying value of our non-marketable equity investment in Altera is classified within equity investments in the Consolidated Condensed Balance Sheets and was $ 3.1 billion as of September 26, 2026 ($ 3.2 billion as of December 27, 2025).
Approximately $ 2.1 billion of the gain resulted from the remeasurement of our non-marketable equity investment in Altera to its fair value at the transaction close date.
On April 8, 2026, we reacquired Apollo's 49 % minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP for aggregate cash consideration of $ 14.2 billion, inclusive of transaction costs.

In connection with our repurchase of the 49 % minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP, discussed within "Note 3: Non-Controlling Interests" within Notes to Consolidated Condensed Financial Statements, we executed and drew on a $ 6.5 billion 364-day senior unsecured term loan facility with an interest rate of 4.79 % in the second quarter of 2026.

Cash used for investing activities in the first nine months of 2026 was higher compared to the first nine months of 2025, primarily due to higher purchases of short-term investments, net of sales and maturities, lower proceeds from capital-related government incentives, cash used for the acquisition of Mentee Robotics and lower inflows from other investing, as well as the absence of proceeds from the divestiture of our Altera and NAND memory businesses received in the first nine months of 2025.
Contributions and distributions made between Arizona SCIP and investors are generally made based on our and Brookfield's proportional ownership interest in Arizona SCIP.

We deconsolidated Altera from our Consolidated Condensed Balance Sheets at the September 12, 2025 transaction close date and account for our retained minority investment in Altera under the equity method of accounting.

Our non-recurring fair value measurements include the valuation of our non-marketable equity investment in Altera which, as of the transaction close date of September 12, 2025, was classified as Level 3.

R&D expenses were $259 million, or 8%, higher in Q3 2026 as compared to Q3 2025, driven by investments in our process technology and products and higher incentive-based cash compensation in Q3 2026, partially offset by lower expenses in Q3 2026 as a result of the Q3 2025 deconsolidation of Altera.

These cash favorable movements were partially offset by partner distributions made to Apollo in connection with our repurchase of the 49% minority ownership interest in Ireland SCIP, repayments of term debt, lower net proceeds from common stock and warrant issuances, lower proceeds from Escrowed Shares, higher payments on finance leases, higher restricted stock unit withholdings and the absence of proceeds from sales of subsidiary shares received in the first nine months of 2025.

s.t: As described in the introduction of this MD&A section, in the second half of 2025 we entered into and concluded upon certain investing and financing transactions, including the Altera divestiture and retained equity investment, an amendment to our CHIPS Act commercial agreement that accelerated $5.7 billion of funding to us, and private placement share sales agreements.

We established the fair value of our non-marketable equity investment in reference to Altera's equity value per the terms of the transaction agreement as the transaction negotiated with SLP represented an orderly transaction between market participants.

The decrease in cash used for investing activities in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily due to lower capital expenditures, higher proceeds from the divestitures of our Altera and NAND memory businesses, and other cash-favorable investing activity, in each case in 2025 as compared to 2024.

Our sale of a 51 % controlling stake in Altera, which is partially offset by the cash sold with Altera, separation and employee-related costs we agreed to fund to SLP, as well as direct and incremental costs we incurred to sell the business, resulted in a pre-tax gain of $ 5.6 billion recognized within interest and other, net in 2025.

Upon closing the transaction, we deconsolidated Altera from our Consolidated Financial Statements and retained a 49% minority investment in Altera which we accounted for under the equity method of accounting.
As of September 12, 2025, our retained interest in Altera is accounted for as an equity method investment.
Contributions and distributions made between Arizona SCIP and investors are generally made based on our and Brookfield's proportional ownership interest in Arizona SCIP.
Our retained interest in Altera is accounted for under the equity method and classified within e quity investments in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
